prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2001 – “Time for Common Sense” (Summary)

Core vision:
- Trust people over government; cut interference and bureaucracy; back families, enterprise, and local institutions. Protect national independence and strengthen communities.

Family and education:
- Tax cuts for families: higher Children’s Tax Credit for under-5s; new Married Couple’s Allowance (transfer unused allowance where there are children under 11 or caring); untax Widowed Parent’s Allowances; reform Working Families Tax Credit to be paid to the caring parent; “Family Scholarships” for parents returning to work.
- Schools: “Free Schools” with full autonomy for heads/governors; simpler exclusions with external Progress Centres for disruptive pupils; more funding to schools by cutting bureaucracy; expand successful schools; allow new faith/parent/charitable schools; parents can trigger Ofsted and management change.
- Students/universities: no top‑up fees; loan repayments only above £20k income; create permanent university endowments for independence.

Law and order:
- More police; slash paperwork; visible policing (“cops in shops”); parish constables; tackle antisocial behaviour.
- Expand secure training places for persistent young offenders; tougher action on drugs (mandatory jail for selling to under‑16s; stiffer sentences near schools).
- Honest sentencing (end automatic early release); prisoners to work and pay reparations; lifetime supervision option for sex offenders; protect children online.
- Victims’ rights: named case officers; explanations for dropped/reduced charges; reform self‑defence and double jeopardy.

Economy, tax and regulation:
- Keep the pound; strengthen fiscal/monetary transparency and discipline; spending growth within trend.
- £8bn annual tax cuts funded by savings outside schools/NHS/police/defence. Measures include: abolish tax on most savings/dividends; raise pensioner allowance by £2,000 (1m out of tax); new Married Couple’s Allowance; boost Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; cut petrol/diesel duty by at least 6p; abolish IR35; business rates cuts; targeted regeneration and share option reliefs.
- Simpler, more transparent taxes (CGT reform). Deregulation Commission with shrinking “regulatory budgets”; small business exemptions; scrap Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear.

Health:
- Match NHS spending plans but end political micromanagement. Patient’s Guarantee: maximum waits by clinical need (starting with cancer/cardiac), with right to treatment elsewhere (including private) if breached.
- Restore ward authority (Ward Sisters, Matrons); GP/patient choice of hospital; proven complementary therapies; remove tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable; better hospice funding; standalone surgical units; expand practice nurse roles; Exceptional Medicines Fund for high‑cost drugs.

Pensioners and care:
- Abolish most savings tax; raise age allowance by £2,000; increase basic pension with extra for over‑75s; optional consolidation of winter fuel/TV/bonus into tax‑free pension.
- Optional funded pensions for younger workers; end compulsory annuity at 75; free nursing care; protect assets for those who pre‑fund long‑term care.

Nation, defence and foreign policy:
- In Europe, not run by Europe: keep veto; reject/renegotiate Nice; reserved powers in UK law; complete single market; combat EU waste/fraud.
- Defence: back NATO; oppose EU army outside NATO; fix overstretch and manning; exempt forces from ECHR; support US missile defence; maintain nuclear deterrent.
- Aid/trade: work towards 0.7% GNP; double charity‑channelled aid; reform EU aid; push trans‑Atlantic FTA toward global free trade by 2020; new Foreign, Commonwealth and Trade Office.
- Asylum: secure reception centres for all new applicants; safe‑country rule; dedicated removals agency.

Society and welfare:
- Office of Civil Society; abolish charities’ irrecoverable VAT (funded from euro‑prep budgets).
- Replace New Deal with “Britain Works,” paying providers for sustained jobs; “Can Work, Must Work” guarantee; lone parents with children 11+ to seek suitable work.
- Better deal for disabled (higher savings disregard; rehab-focused Incapacity Benefit agency). National anti‑fraud task force; clean up National Insurance numbers.

Town, country and transport:
- Foot and Mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP; cut rural business rates; protect post offices via benefit card; no gold‑plating EU rules; clear food labelling; animal welfare.
- End national/regional housebuilding targets; empower councils; protect waters with “Blue Belts.”
- Urban renewal via local Regeneration Companies; tougher action on antisocial tenants; promote brownfield building; expand homeownership (right‑to‑buy discounts, rent‑to‑mortgage).
- Transport: invest in roads/rail; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe; charge foreign lorries (Brit Disc); cut fuel duty 6p; pro‑competition rail revival; tech‑led emissions cuts.

Culture and media:
- £3bn cultural endowment (funded by Channel 4 privatisation and Lottery surpluses); simpler Lottery rules; boost tourism promotion.
- Sport: protect school sport time/playing fields; charitable status for clubs; streamline funding.
- Media: privatise Channel 4 (retain PSB remit); single converged regulator; liberalise ownership; fair BBC oversight; fair access for religious broadcasters.

Democracy and governance:
- Empower effective “free councils”; local referendums for big tax rises; abolish regional agencies/assemblies.
- English Votes for English Laws; strengthen Lords via independent appointments and pursue reform with elected element; stronger select committees; PM to face Commons twice weekly; retain FPTP.
- Support Belfast Agreement and security in Northern Ireland.
- Fewer ministers, MPs (after scrutiny reforms), and special advisers; scrap regional tiers.
